is the purpose of the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU) for an EPIRB?

chosen.content: The excerpt provides guidelines for the proper storage and maintenance of EPIRBs and SARTs on a vessel. First, stow the EPIRB in its dedicated bracket; Then, arm the Hydrostatic Release Unit (HRU); Next, visually check the bracket and HRU for corrosion or expiry; After that, stow the SART or AIS-SART close to the liferaft or grab bag; Finally, keep the SART switched off until needed; Then, test the SART only per the manufacturer's specified test procedure; Then, mount the SART as high as practical once activated. This follows GMDSS, Cospas-Sarsat. Be careful: a seized bracket or expired HRU can prevent automatic release. Done correctly, the EPIRB and SART are readily accessible and functional in an emergency.

What should I do if I hear a Mayday call?

chosen.content: Boaters can use VHF radio to communicate distress calls in emergencies. First, tune VHF to channel 16; Then, make a Mayday call; Next, speak 'MAYDAY' three times; After that, say 'THIS IS' once; Finally, state the vessel name three times and call sign once; Then, repeat 'MAYDAY' and vessel name once; Then, provide vessel position and movement details; Then, describe the nature of distress and assistance needed; Then, state the number of persons onboard; Then, provide any additional relevant information; Then, end with 'OVER'. Use Channel 16. Use the prowords MAYDAY, OVER, THIS IS as appropriate. Be careful: do not transmit on a distress channel unless you are able to assist. Done correctly, rescue services are alerted to the distress situation.

What should I do upon hearing a SECURITE broadcast?
